q: Collatz conjecture: start from any positive integer n. If n is even, divide it by 2; if n is odd, replace it with 3n+1. Repeating this, does every starting value eventually reach 1?
computable_special_case: Given one starting integer n, compute its Collatz trajectory and check whether it reaches 1 within a chosen step bound — a decidable per-instance check (the conjecture is that this always succeeds for every n, which remains unproven despite verification up to roughly 2^71).

q: Goldbach's conjecture: can every even integer greater than 2 be written as the sum of two prime numbers?
attribution: Christian Goldbach (1742, in a letter to Euler)
computable_special_case: Given one even integer m > 2, search primes p <= m/2 for a prime pair (p, m-p) — a decidable per-instance search (verified by computer up to 4x10^18; unproven in general).

q: Twin prime conjecture: are there infinitely many primes p such that p+2 is also prime?
attribution: attributed to Euclid; formalized as a Landau problem (1912)
computable_special_case: Given a bound N, count twin-prime pairs below N by trial division or a sieve — a finite, bounded SEARCH, not a single decidable existence check; it cannot settle infinitude by itself (Zhang 2013 and the Polymath project proved a finite bounded gap occurs infinitely often, currently 246, but not gap=2).

q: Legendre's conjecture: does there always exist at least one prime number strictly between n^2 and (n+1)^2, for every positive integer n?
attribution: Adrien-Marie Legendre (early 19th century); one of Landau's problems
computable_special_case: Given one n, search the finite integer range (n^2, (n+1)^2) for a prime by trial division — a decidable per-instance check (a 2026 result proves a related bound under the unproven Riemann Hypothesis, but Legendre's conjecture itself remains open).

q: Erdős–Straus conjecture: for every integer n >= 2, can 4/n be written as a sum of three positive unit fractions 1/x + 1/y + 1/z (x, y, z positive integers)?
attribution: Paul Erdős and Ernst G. Straus (1948)
computable_special_case: Given one n, search bounded ranges of x, y, z for a valid decomposition of 4/n — a decidable, bounded per-instance search (verified by computer for all n up to 10^18; unproven in general).

q: Lonely runner conjecture: if k runners with pairwise distinct constant speeds run laps on a circular track of unit length starting at the same point, does every runner eventually become 'lonely' — at distance at least 1/k (measured around the track) from every other runner — at some moment in time?
computable_special_case: For a SPECIFIC small runner count k with specific speeds, numerically search over time for the loneliest moment of the slowest-tracked runner — a bounded per-instance check. The general conjecture (all k) is proven true only for k <= 12 as of this check (k=7 through 12 all settled in 2025-2026); k=13 is the first open case, per https://www.quantamagazine.org/new-strides-made-on-deceptively-simple-lonely-runner-problem-20260306/ (accessed for this tranche).

q: Beal's conjecture: if A^x + B^y = C^z where A, B, C, x, y, z are positive integers and x, y, z are all greater than 2, must A, B, and C share a common prime factor?
computable_special_case: Given bounded ranges for A, B, C, x, y, z, search for a counterexample (a solution where A, B, C share no common prime factor) — a bounded SEARCH, not a single decidable check; a US$1,000,000 AMS-administered prize for a refereed proof or counterexample remains unclaimed.

q: Does an odd perfect number exist — an odd positive integer equal to the sum of its proper divisors (divisors excluding itself)?
attribution: traced to Euclid/Nicomachus-era antiquity; a standing open question
computable_special_case: Given one odd candidate integer, sum its proper divisors and compare to the candidate — a decidable per-instance check (no odd perfect number exists below roughly 10^2000, computationally, but existence in general is unresolved).

q: Riemann hypothesis: do all non-trivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function have real part exactly 1/2?
computable_special_case: Given a height bound T, numerically verify that every non-trivial zero with imaginary part below T lies on the critical line Re(s)=1/2 — a bounded numerical verification (done for the first many billions of zeros), not a proof of the general hypothesis, which is a Clay Millennium Prize Problem and remains open despite recurring claimed proofs (several new ones circulated in 2026 alone, none accepted).

q: Union-closed sets conjecture (Frankl's conjecture): for every finite family of sets that is closed under taking unions (and contains at least one non-empty set), must some element belong to at least half of the sets in the family?
computable_special_case: Given one small, explicitly listed union-closed family of sets, check by brute force whether some element appears in at least half the sets — a decidable per-instance check (Gilmer's 2022 breakthrough proved every such family has SOME element in at least a fixed small fraction of the sets, later improved past 38%, but the full 'at least half' conjecture remains open).
